name: Frankfort
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Frankfort, IL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Frankfort, IL: Lighting of the Green, Holidays on the Green with reindeer and carriage rides, and a lantern parade downtown.
lede: Frankfort keeps Christmas close to home on Breidert Green, the downtown park beside the Old Plank Road Trail. The village lights the green each December, then fills it with carriage rides, reindeer and a lantern parade from the history museum.
celebrates: Frankfort celebrates in two big steps on Breidert Green. First comes the annual Lighting of the Green, when the mayor and Village Board count down to the grand illumination with choir music, free hot cocoa and cookies, a light projection on the Grainery Tower, and Santa and Mrs. Claus. Later in the month, Holidays on the Green brings horse-drawn carriage rides, a trackless train, live reindeer and caroling, all free. The Frankfort Area Historical Society adds a lantern parade and its Candlelight House Walk, while the Park District runs Letters to Santa and a Santa workshop for little ones.
lastyear: In 2025 the village called its weekend festival Home For The Holidays and held it on Breidert Green from noon to 5 p.m. on December 13 and 14. Patch reported that Saturday brought trackless train rides, real reindeer, Santa and Mrs. Claus, horse and carriage rides, cookies, hot cocoa and a lantern parade. Sunday added live holiday shows on the Breidert Green stage and characters strolling downtown. Earlier, on December 4, the Lighting of the Green featured school choirs and photos with decorated police, fire and public works vehicles.
facts: Breidert Green is named for Burton Breidert, Frankfort's first village administrator. It was dedicated in 1986 and rebuilt in 2014, and its stage sits right on the Old Plank Road Trail, just east of the Grainery that towers over the park. Frankfort's downtown began in 1855 along the Joliet and Northern Indiana Railroad, and the village incorporated in 1879. The historical society's Candlelight House Walk, its biggest fundraiser, is now in its 45th year, and in 2024 a $250,000 state grant was announced to help save the downtown water tower.
trains: Breidert Green sits right beside an old railroad line. The Old Plank Road Trail follows the Joliet and Northern Indiana Railroad, later run by the Michigan Central, whose service ended in 1972; the paved 22 mile trail opened in 1997. Frankfort has no Metra stop of its own, and the village points riders to Rock Island stations in Tinley Park, New Lenox and Mokena's Hickory Creek, plus Metra Electric at Richton Park. The Frankfort Park District also runs a Polar Express Storytime Train from Hickory Creek that rides to the North Pole to bring back Santa.

traditions: The mayor and Village Board lead the countdown that lights up Breidert Green, with choir music, cocoa, cookies and Santa.
A free afternoon of carriage rides, a trackless train, live reindeer, Santa visits and community caroling on the green.
Children pick up a free glowing lantern at the historical museum on Kansas Street and parade through downtown to Breidert Green.
The Frankfort Area Historical Society opens decorated homes for tours, with homemade Christmas cookies served at the museum.
The Park District reads The Polar Express aboard a train from Hickory Creek station and brings Santa back from the North Pole.
Santa's mailbox appears at the Founders Community Center, and Santa writes back to Park District families who mail him a wish list.
kidfact: The path next to Breidert Green used to be a railroad, and before that it was planned as a road made of wooden planks that was never built.
faq: Where do Frankfort's Christmas celebrations happen?

Most of them happen on Breidert Green in historic downtown Frankfort, the park at 432 W Nebraska Street beside the Old Plank Road Trail. The Lighting of the Green and Holidays on the Green both take place there, and the lantern parade ends there after starting at the Frankfort Area Historical Society museum at 132 Kansas Street.
Are Frankfort's village Christmas events free?

Yes. The Village of Frankfort lists Holidays on the Green as free, including carriage rides, the trackless train, the live reindeer and visits with Santa, and it serves free hot chocolate and cookies. The Lighting of the Green also offers free cocoa and cookies, and the village invites families to bring a canned good for neighbors in need.
What is the Frankfort lantern parade?

The Frankfort Area Historical Society leads a lantern parade as the sun sets during Holidays on the Green. Children gather at the museum on Kansas Street, collect a free glowing lantern and walk through historic downtown to Breidert Green, where families sing carols and warm up with cocoa and cookies near a fire.
Can we see Santa in Frankfort?

Yes, in several places. Santa and Mrs. Claus greet families and pose for photos at the Lighting of the Green and visit again during Holidays on the Green. The Frankfort Park District also hosts a Santa Photos and Workshop morning at the Founders Community Center with crafts, games and cookie decorating, and registration is required.
Is there a Christmas train near Frankfort?

Yes. The Frankfort Park District runs a Polar Express Storytime Train that leaves from the Hickory Creek Metra station in Mokena, with elves, the story, cookies and music, and Santa rides back with the children. It is open to Park District residents first through a lottery and fills up quickly, so watch for registration in the fall.
